_comment: Coordinates are in PDF points, measured from the TOP-LEFT of the page (pdfplumber convention: x0/x1 = left/right, top/bottom = distance from top). generate_lir.py converts these to reportlab's bottom-left origin automatically. All four templates share the same header layout (Route / Flight number / A/C Registration / Date / STD (LT) / Load control signature) but differ slightly in hold count, hold coordinates, and page height, so each is listed independently. Each template has two hold diagrams: the top 'LOADING INSTRUCTION' diagram (one box per hold, no PCS/KGS split -- this is where the standard load pattern gets written, since it's telling ramp staff what to load) and the bottom 'LOADING REPORT' diagram (separate PCS and KGS boxes per hold -- this stays blank for ramp staff to fill in by hand after loading, confirming what actually went on). 'instruction_hold_boxes' below are the top-diagram boxes; the bottom-diagram PCS/KGS boxes are intentionally not filled by this skill.

act_code_map._comment: Maps the 'ACT' aircraft-type code seen in flight schedules to a template key below. Extend this if a new code shows up (e.g. a dedicated XLR code) or if a different data source uses different codes (some use ICAO codes like A20N/A21N/A21X instead).

A321_XLR.label: A321 XLR
A321_XLR._note: No standard load pattern has been confirmed for XLR yet (no XLR tail currently rotates through BGY). Leave default_pattern null until confirmed -- the script will leave the instruction boxes blank and flag it rather than guess.
